messages:
alice: Noticed a recurring pattern on the KV cache today — tenant 'acme-pay' kept growing its residency over long contexts and pushed other tenants into paging. p95 CPU and tail latencies spiked on shared pool. Anyone else seeing cross-tenant impact?

bob: Yep, saw it around 11:02. Long chat sessions with streaming + function calls. KV entries never got evicted because access pattern looked like 'hot' due to long-lived KV refs.

carol: Can you paste the profile? curious if it's fragmentation (lots of small pages) or outright resident pages.

alice: Paste from the live profiler (snipped):

```
kv_stats: {
  total_pages: 118k,
  resident_by_tenant: {acme-pay: 45k, beta-1: 12k, internal-obs: 8k, others: 53k},
  page_frag_pct: 22%,
  avg_page_age_secs: 4200,
  eviction_ops_last_hour: 320
}
hot_accesses: acme-pay: 92% read-hot during streaming longctx
memory_growth: acme-pay: +6GB over 2h
```

alice: That + the p95 token latency bump from perf-bot below.

perf-bot: rolling 15m: p50=18ms p95=123ms p99=410ms, host_cpu=78% (shared-pool-7)

dave: From heap profiler there's a lot of small fragments due to variable-sized KV objects created by the tokenizer cache layer. Reuse is low because keys include session-specific metadata. We should normalize key shapes.

erin: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) soft per-tenant page quota + background compaction when tenant under quota; 2) aggressive time-decay eviction for pages not accessed in X minutes (but we need to tune X so longcontexts don't lose very recent tokens).

frank: For canary, we can flip a config flag: `kv.max_pages_per_tenant=30k` and `kv.decay_window_sec=1800` for 10% traffic and measure impact on p95 and paging. Command to run sim harness: `./run_kv_isolation_sim --tenants 500 --workload longctx:0.12,chat:0.6`

carol: Important to check fragmentation compaction cost — full compaction pauses were ~120ms in POC. Need to bound compaction CPU so SLOs don't break. Maybe do incremental compaction slices (25ms).

alice: Agreed. Also think about KV key canonicalization to improve reuse. If we can collapse session-metadata suffixes we reduce unique pages. Proposal: add a hashing/canonicalization step in front of KV put.

bob: I ran a quick microbench: canonicalize -> reuse up 3.7x, fragmentation down 12%. But canonicalization CPU adds ~6% per op. tradeoff looks acceptable for longrunning sessions.

erin: Plan: 1) small canary (10%) with `max_pages_per_tenant=30k` + `decay_window=1800` + incremental compaction slice=25ms; 2) A/B on canonicalization flag across another 10% group; 3) collect p95/p99, eviction_ops, page_frag_pct, resident_by_tenant histograms.

frank: I'll schedule the canary for tomorrow 09:00 UTC. I'll also add a dashboard tile that breaks down resident_by_tenant and a noisy-neighbor alert when one tenant accounts for >30% of shared-pool residency for 10m.

dave: Note: when we force-evict pages we should prefer LRU within tenant but also prefer churn candidates (low reuse score). Add reuse_score in eviction decision.

alice: Good. Whoever drives the canary, please post results here. If we see compaction costs spike, rollback compaction slice and rely on decay. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
